Bayesian UAV, Satellite, and Field Phenotyping

bayesAgriFlow

Source: vignettes/v37-uav-satellite-phenotyping.Rmd
v37-uav-satellite-phenotyping.Rmd

Purpose

This vignette develops the modeling layer introduced in version 1.3.0. UAV and satellite variables are treated as predictors measured over experimental units, while the biological response remains explicit. High-throughput phenotyping is valuable because it can repeatedly characterize crop status at scale, but the statistical model must still respect blocks, plots, repeated acquisitions, spatial structure, and calibration (Yang et al. 2017).

1. Start with the estimand

Before specifying a model, state the quantity of scientific interest. Examples include expected plot biomass at a given date, cultivar differences after adjusting for canopy features, or the probability that predicted stress exceeds an intervention threshold. This prevents the remote-sensing feature set from defining the question after the fact.

Interpretation checklist

  • Write the response and target population first.
  • State whether the goal is explanation, prediction, screening, or decision support.
  • Separate sensor convenience from scientific relevance.

2. The bayes_rs_model() constructor

bayes_rs_model() creates a bayes_design of type remote_sensing. Numeric sensor features become explicit fixed predictors. Optional fixed terms can add experimental factors. Coordinates activate a two-dimensional Gaussian process unless spatial = FALSE is requested.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("uav")
des <- bayes_rs_model(
  d, response = "biomass",
  predictors = c("ndvi", "ndre", "canopy_height"),
  fixed = ~ cultivar,
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", block = "block"
)
bayes_plan(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Inspect bayes_plan() before fitting.
  • Use predictors that are available at prediction time.
  • Avoid including variables that leak the target response.

3. Phenotyping convenience wrapper

bayes_rs_phenotype() is a semantic wrapper around the same model constructor. It records the target trait but does not invent a separate fitting engine. This makes code easier to read while preserving one model architecture.

phen <- bayes_rs_phenotype(
  d, trait = "biomass",
  features = c("ndvi", "canopy_height"),
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", block = "block"
)
phen$model_options$phenotype_trait

Interpretation checklist

  • Use trait names that refer to biological outcomes.
  • Do not call an uncalibrated index a phenotype unless the scientific meaning is explicit.

4. Experimental blocks remain part of the model

A UAV may observe all plots at once, but randomization and blocking remain properties of the field experiment. Remote sensing does not erase them. Grouping terms are retained through the common design-aware infrastructure.

des_block <- bayes_rs_model(
  d, "biomass", c("ndvi", "canopy_height"),
  block = "block", spatial = FALSE
)
bayes_design_audit(des_block)

Interpretation checklist

  • Keep blocks when they belong to the randomization.
  • Do not replace block effects with spatial smoothing without a design-based reason.
  • Compare spatial and design terms by scientific role, not only predictive score.

5. Spatial field adjustment

When plot coordinates are available and local residual structure is plausible, the model can add a two-dimensional Gaussian-process term. This route reuses the spatial and spatiotemporal architecture already established in versions 0.5.0 and 1.2.0.

des_sp <- bayes_rs_model(
  d, "biomass", c("ndvi", "ndre"),
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", block = "block",
  spatial = TRUE, spatial_cov = "matern32"
)
bayes_plan(des_sp)

Interpretation checklist

  • Spatial smoothing should address residual dependence, not conceal treatment structure.
  • Check coordinate scale and number of unique locations.
  • Report the covariance specification.

6. Temporal satellite model

Repeated satellite acquisitions can use the same model with an explicit time role. Version 1.3.0 supports no temporal effect, linear time, factor time, and an AR(1) route for repeated series. This is intentionally narrower than claiming a universal remote-sensing time-series engine.

sat <- bayes_teaching_data("satellite")
des_t <- bayes_rs_model(
  sat, "biomass", c("ndvi", "evi"),
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", time = "day",
  subject = "location_id", temporal = "ar1"
)
bayes_plan(des_t)

Interpretation checklist

  • Use a subject or series identifier for repeated observations.
  • Do not treat acquisition date as independent replication.
  • State whether prediction is temporal interpolation or forecasting.

7. Priors remain a model decision

The constructor describes structure; priors remain handled by the existing prior layer. Sensor features may be standardized upstream when that makes prior scales easier to justify. Priors should represent plausible effects on the response scale and should be checked with prior predictive simulation.

if (FALSE) {
  pr <- bayes_prior(strategy = "regularizing")
  fit <- bayes_fit(des, prior = pr, engine = "brms", compute = bayes_compute(backend = "cmdstanr"))
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Do not select priors solely to accelerate sampling.
  • Use prior predictive checks to identify implausible response scales.
  • Document transformations of predictors.

8. Fitting through the common engine

Heavy estimation remains optional. The intended route is brms with cmdstanr or rstan as configured by the user. bayesAgriFlow never installs CmdStan or Python silently.

if (FALSE) {
  ctrl <- bayes_compute(n_cpus = 8, chains = 4, backend = "cmdstanr")
  fit <- bayes_fit(des, engine = "brms", compute = ctrl)
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Check capability status before fitting.
  • Record backend and version.
  • Use enough effective samples for the reported quantities.

9. Diagnostics before interpretation

Remote-sensing models can be high-dimensional and spatially structured. Convergence and effective-sample diagnostics therefore come before biological interpretation. Posterior predictive checks should be evaluated by treatment, time, and spatial region when those dimensions matter.

if (FALSE) {
  bayes_diagnose(fit)
  bayes_pp_check(fit)
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Resolve divergences rather than ignoring them.
  • Inspect R-hat, ESS, and Monte Carlo error.
  • Use conditional PPCs when global checks can hide local misfit.

10. Posterior phenotypic prediction

bayes_rs_predict() delegates to the stable prediction layer and adds remote-sensing provenance. Predictions can target posterior means or posterior predictive observations. The former estimates the expected response; the latter includes observation noise.

if (FALSE) {
  pred_mean <- bayes_rs_predict(fit, type = "mean")
  pred_obs  <- bayes_rs_predict(fit, type = "predictive")
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Choose prediction type before comparing uncertainty.
  • Do not call a predictive interval a confidence interval.
  • Keep prediction data attached to map-ready output.

11. Out-of-sample evaluation

Predictive performance should be evaluated on a partition that reflects intended use. Randomly splitting pixels from the same plot across training and validation can exaggerate performance. Site, date, block, or plot-level holdouts may be more appropriate depending on the target.

Interpretation checklist

  • Partition at the scientific independence level.
  • Avoid leakage between repeated acquisitions of the same unit.
  • Report how the test set differs from training data.

12. UAV versus satellite scale

UAV and satellite products differ in spatial resolution, revisit interval, spectral response, and geolocation error. Their numerical variables should not be assumed exchangeable simply because both are called NDVI. Multi-sensor fusion is therefore explicit rather than automatic.

Interpretation checklist

  • Record sensor and platform.
  • Check spatial-support mismatch.
  • Model systematic sensor differences when needed.

13. Threshold decisions

A practical phenotyping task may ask whether a trait exceeds a threshold rather than only requesting a mean prediction. Posterior draws can directly estimate such probabilities, which are more decision-relevant than coloring a map by fitted mean alone.

if (FALSE) {
  pred <- bayes_rs_predict(fit)
  risk <- bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred, threshold = 5, direction = "above")
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Choose thresholds before inspecting posterior probabilities when possible.
  • State the consequence associated with threshold exceedance.
  • Avoid converting a continuous posterior to a binary label without reporting uncertainty.

14. Model comparison

Remote-sensing feature sets can be compared with the package’s existing predictive model-comparison tools. A larger model is not automatically better. Model comparison should consider predictive adequacy, collinearity, interpretability, and whether variables are available in deployment.

if (FALSE) {
  bayes_compare_models(fit_ndvi, fit_multi)
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Compare models fitted to the same outcome and observations.
  • Prefer out-of-sample predictive criteria for prediction questions.
  • Do not interpret model weights as effect sizes.

15. Reporting a phenotyping analysis

A complete report should state the experimental design, sensor/platform, preprocessing, spatial support, biological response, predictor definitions, priors, backend, diagnostics, prediction target, validation strategy, and posterior uncertainty. The remote-sensing map is an output, not a substitute for this information.

Interpretation checklist

  • Report calibration and validation separately.
  • Describe spatial and temporal structure explicitly.
  • Distinguish estimation from prediction and decision quantities.

16. Minimal integrated workflow

The recommended workflow remains deliberately compact at the top level even though each stage is auditable.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("uav")
des <- bayes_rs_phenotype(d, "biomass", c("ndvi", "ndre", "canopy_height"), x_coord="x", y_coord="y", block="block")
plan <- bayes_plan(des)
if (FALSE) {
  fit <- bayes_fit(des, engine="brms", compute=bayes_compute(backend="cmdstanr"))
  bayes_diagnose(fit)
  pred <- bayes_rs_predict(fit)
  bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred)
}

Interpretation checklist

  • Design first.
  • Fit second.
  • Diagnose before interpreting.
  • Predict at the intended support.
  • Report uncertainty and provenance.

Summary

The 1.3.0 phenotyping layer is intentionally conservative: it provides a unified Bayesian model for analysis-ready sensor features while preserving experimental design, spatial/temporal dependence, and posterior uncertainty. It does not make image-derived variables biologically valid by declaration. Calibration, experimental support, validation design, and model diagnostics remain scientific responsibilities.

Phenotyping model audit worksheet

Before interpreting a fitted model, answer these questions explicitly.

  1. What biological response is being predicted?
  2. Which sensor variables enter as predictors?
  3. Which experimental factors enter as design terms?
  4. What is the randomization unit?
  5. Is spatial smoothing scientifically justified?
  6. Is time modeled as a trend, factor, or dependent process?
  7. Are repeated acquisitions identified by subject or series?
  8. Were predictor scales transformed or standardized?
  9. Are priors interpretable on the resulting model scale?
  10. Did prior predictive simulation cover plausible biological values?
  11. Did all MCMC diagnostic gates pass?
  12. Was predictive performance evaluated on independent scientific units?
  13. Does the validation set represent intended deployment?
  14. Are predictions expected responses or future observations?
  15. Are threshold probabilities tied to a meaningful agronomic decision?

The worksheet is intentionally separate from automated model output. A model cannot determine whether its own biological target and validation design are appropriate.

Yang, Guijun, Jiangang Liu, Chunjiang Zhao, et al. 2017. “Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Remote Sensing for Field-Based Crop Phenotyping: Current Status and Perspectives.” Frontiers in Plant Science 8: 1111. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2017.01111.
